title: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia powers Asian AI stock rally
excerpt: Asia is central to Nvidia's AI supply chain, from Taiwan's advanced chipmaking to South Korea's memory chips and Japan's semiconductor equipment.
content_html:
Asian stocks roar back as Jensen Huang's Nvidia return reignites the AI trade

By Huileng Tan

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-24T08:25:53.506Z

Asian stocks rallied sharply on Tuesday after Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia's CEO, lifting shares of companies across the region that supply the US chip giant and the wider AI industry.

South Korea's Kospi jumped as much as 8% in early trading, triggering a five-minute halt in automated buy orders. Samsung Electronics climbed 9%, and SK Hynix surged 11%.

Japan's Nikkei 225 climbed 5%, as memory chipmaker Kioxia rose 11%. Chip equipment makers Advantest and Tokyo Electron gained 16% and 13%, respectively, while tech investor SoftBank Group climbed 8%.

In Taiwan, the benchmark Taiex index surged 9%, with TSMC, Nvidia's main chipmaking partner, hitting its daily 10% price limit.

Asia plays a central role in Nvidia's supply chain. TSMC manufactures its advanced AI processors, while South Korea's SK Hynix and Samsung produce high-bandwidth memory used in AI systems. Japanese companies provide semiconductor manufacturing and testing equipment.

The gains followed heavy losses across Asia's technology sector. Taiwan's benchmark index plunged about 18% last week, while South Korea's Kospi also suffered heavy losses.

The rally extended a dramatic rebound on Wall Street on Monday, when Nvidia shares soared 31.5% after Huang's reinstatement, helping lift the Nasdaq Composite 6.5%.

Huang's return has revived confidence in the AI trade after weeks of selling driven by concerns about the sustainability of AI spending and the financing behind the industry's rapid expansion.

His reinstatement came 11 days after he resigned amid reports of extramarital affairs, including one involving a woman suspected by US intelligence of spying for China.

"Jensen’s return takes away one of the biggest unknowns hanging over the AI trade. He is not just Nvidia’s CEO; he is arguably the biggest salesman for the entire AI ecosystem," wrote Charu Chanana, the chief investment strategist at Saxo, in a Tuesday note.

Vishnu Varathan, head of macro strategy for Asia Pacific at Mizuho, said Huang's return also eased fears that disruptions to Nvidia-backed financing deals could trigger financial distress among smaller AI cloud providers.

Still, the leadership change has not resolved questions about whether the enormous investments flowing into AI infrastructure will generate sufficient returns. US restrictions on advanced chip exports also remain a concern for data center operators serving Chinese customers.

"Jensen’s return repairs confidence, but it doesn't automatically repair the economics of AI spending," Chanana wrote.
